summary: Sen. Mitch McConnell (Republican) retired, so the seat was open. U.S. Rep. Andy Barr (Republican) won, defeating Charles Booker (Democrat) and one independent.

candidates.name: Andy Barr
candidates.bio: Barr graduated from the University of Virginia and received his law degree from the University of Kentucky. He has represented Kentucky's 6th Congressional District in the U.S. House since 2013. He won the May 2026 Republican Senate primary.

positions.summary: Supports tax cuts, citing the 2025 law that he says ended taxes on Social Security benefits, overtime and tips, and a repeal of the estate tax for farmers.
Says he ushered through Congress legislation giving veterans more access to non-VA health care options.
Supports deporting criminal illegal immigrants, restarting border wall construction, funding more border agents and ending catch and release.
Says he wants to bring back coal and lower energy costs, and opposes Green New Deal efforts and ESG mandates.
Voted in 2013 for the Pain-Capable Unborn Child Protection Act, which he said bans abortions nationwide at 20 weeks or later.

candidates.name: Charles Booker
candidates.bio: Booker comes from a West Louisville family and says he grew up rationing insulin. He is a former state representative who lost the 2020 Democratic Senate primary and was the Democratic nominee in 2022 and 2026. Between those races he worked in the office of Gov. Andy Beshear.

positions.summary: Says he would cut taxes for working and middle-class families, protect Social Security and Medicare, and revoke the national emergency used to justify tariffs.
Says he would restore ACA subsidies, create a state-run public option and extend Medicare drug price negotiation to all Kentuckians.
Said on X in November 2025 that "ICE really does need to be abolished."
Says he opposes private school vouchers and Trump administration cuts to Title I and special education funding, and supports raising teacher pay.

Says he would co-sponsor the Ratepayer Protection Act requiring large data centers to cover their utility costs, pursue an all-of-the-above energy strategy, and protect coal miners' pensions and benefits.
Says he respects Kentuckians' 2022 rejection of a constitutional amendment on abortion, would protect access to contraception and IVF, and would ensure emergency care for pregnancy complications.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (political.org Nov 14 tally, AP called 34 of 35). 2026-11-25: shares match The Green Papers. No page confirming certification was found.
